title: THE CALLER
mv: Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.
mvp: “Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.”1 Thessalonians 5:24
assignment: Mention five (5) people called by God in the Bible (5x2=10 marks).

b.x: God has been calling men into purpose from the Old Testament days (Genesis 6:13-14). He is the ultimate Caller because He knows the purpose every human is meant to fulfil. It is important to note that the power of a calling does not lie in the ability of the called but in the faithfulness and sovereignty of the Caller. In this study, we shall examine the nature and attributes of the Caller and how to respond to His calls.

i: The Sovereignty of the Caller: God as the Sovereign Being chooses according to His divine prerogative (1 Samuel 16:1, 11, 13; Romans 9:15-16).

The Holiness of the Caller: God’s nature is holy, hence, He calls His people into holiness (1Peter 1:15-16). As much as He loves His creature, He cannot behold iniquity (Isaiah 1:15-16). In other words, He will only use those who purge themselves of their sins (2 Timothy 2:21). God does not compromise His holiness (Exodus 19:5-6).
The Faithfulness of the Caller: He never abandons His promises (1 Thessalonians 5:24). He finishes what He begins (Philippians 1:6).
The Purposefulness of the Caller: Every call is tied to destiny and divine assignment (Jeremiah 1:5; Romans 8:30).

b.x: As believers grow in their walk with Christ, they must always remember that the focus of their calling is not merely on the assignment but on the Caller Himself. When you fix your eyes on Him, He transforms your life and equips you to fulfil His divine purpose. To respond correctly, believers must:

i: Recognise His Voice: Believers must train their hearts to discern through the word and the Spirit (1 Samuel 3:9-10; John 10:27). The deeper they dig into knowing God, the clearer they will hear and understand His voice.

Obey the Caller: Believers are not expected to only hear God but must obey Him absolutely, even without knowing all the details (Hebrews 11:8). There is a grievous consequence in disobeying the divine call (Jonah 1:1-3, 17; Hebrews 2:2).
Trust His Presence: One thing the called could be assured of is the presence of the Caller. He does not leave His own stranded (Exodus 3:12; Matthew 28:20).
Be alert to transforming encounters: Some specific encounters with the Caller can change the destiny of the called (Acts 10:10-16).

b.x: God, the Caller, will not abandon the called.
